change.requirement_text:
# Requirement #2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

plants.description: Replacing the per-member 'continue' with 'break' terminates the whole property loop, so every property after the first key-kind mismatch is silently dropped from the collected member list.
The ContainsKey guard is inverted: when the int key is already present the dictionary Add throws ArgumentException, and when it is absent the member is never registered at all.
The duplicate check for string-keyed properties now consults the int-key dictionary, so duplicate string keys are no longer detected and the subsequent Add throws ArgumentException.
For an int-keyed field, member.StringKey is null, so the guard calls stringMembers.ContainsKey(null) which throws ArgumentNullException and aborts analysis of the type.
Removes the registration of int-keyed properties into intMembers, so the analyzer no longer has the member/key mapping it needs and produces incomplete results.
Removes the registration of string-keyed properties into stringMembers, so those members are missing from the analyzer's collected member set.
Removes the registration of int-keyed fields into intMembers, so the analyzer no longer resolves the key mapping for those fields.
Removes the registration of string-keyed fields into stringMembers, leaving those members out of the collected member set the analyzer relies on.
Uses the indexer instead of Add; with the ContainsKey guard in place the behaviour is identical.
Uses the indexer instead of Add; with the ContainsKey guard in place the behaviour is identical.
Passes the same arguments by name; the call is unchanged.
Compares the ContainsKey result against false instead of negating it; logically identical.

findings.message: When adding a string key member, the guard checks `!intMembers.ContainsKey(member.IntKey)` instead of `!stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)`. This checks the wrong dictionary and the wrong key type, so string members can be incorrectly skipped or retained based on unrelated int-key state, corrupting the key map.

The duplicate-key guard for string members here correctly uses `stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)`, which is inconsistent with the buggy version at lines 1038-1042 and indicates the earlier block was likely a copy-paste error.

The analyzer tests define the expected behavior for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` (report MsgPack004/003/005/015, suppress MsgPack011/016/017), but no analyzer code changes are included in the pull request. The only code change is in the source generator's TypeCollector.cs. Without modifications to the analyzer to inspect `SuppressSourceGeneration` and adjust diagnostic reporting, the analyzer behavior will not change and these tests will fail.
Documents the intended analyzer behavior for suppressed types, but documentation alone does not implement the fix.

findings.message: In the first code block, `stringMembers.Add(member.StringKey, (member, item.Type))` is removed without a `ContainsKey` guard or replacement. This means string-keyed members in that code path are no longer tracked for duplicate detection, so duplicate string keys would go unreported. The second block (around line 1164) correctly adds the `ContainsKey` check, making the omission in the first block inconsistent and likely a defect.

The TypeCollector.cs changes are generic robustness improvements (ContainsKey checks before Add, continue after reporting mismatched-key-kind diagnostic) and do not reference SuppressSourceGeneration, so I cannot tell whether they fix the reported issue or whether the actual fix is missing from the shown changes.

The diff does not show the code change that makes the analyzer process types with SuppressSourceGeneration = true. The only production code change is in TypeCollector.cs and concerns key-collision handling (continue on mismatch, ContainsKey before Add); it does not reference SuppressSourceGeneration. Without seeing the analyzer logic that was skipping suppressed types, it cannot be determined whether the requirement is met.

The changes shown do not include the actual SuppressSourceGeneration implementation. The tests expect that (a) the source generator skips formatter generation for suppressed types, and (b) the analyzer suppresses MsgPack011/MsgPack016/MsgPack017 for suppressed types while still reporting other diagnostics. None of that logic is visible in the modified files shown. The TypeCollector.cs changes only make key-collection resilient to duplicate keys (preventing crashes), and the README/tests document and verify the expected behavior. I cannot determine whether the SuppressSourceGeneration checks already exist elsewhere in the codebase or are missing from this PR.

findings.message: The changes at lines 1008, 1022-1026, and 1038-1042 do not reference SuppressSourceGeneration and do not modify analyzer behavior based on this property. They only add duplicate-key robustness (conditional dictionary adds and a continue after reporting mixed-key diagnostic). The reported issue that the analyzer does not work with SuppressSourceGeneration = true is not addressed.
The changes at lines 1148, 1162-1166, and 1179-1182 have the same problem: they add duplicate-key robustness but do not check SuppressSourceGeneration or alter analyzer behavior for suppressed types.

The test SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed expects that MsgPack011, MsgPack016, and MsgPack017 are not reported for suppressed types, but no code change is shown in the analyzer that implements this skipping behavior.

The tests verify analyzer behavior for suppressed types, but no code change is shown that checks the SuppressSourceGeneration property on [MessagePackObject] or adjusts analyzer behavior accordingly. Without this, the analyzer cannot know to treat suppressed types differently.
